questions.question: What does it mean for $\mathcal{C} = \{G_i:i\in I\}$ to be a cover of $E\subseteq X$?
questions.explanation: A collection $\mathcal{C}=\{G_i:i\in I\}$ is a cover of $E\subseteq X$ when $E\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in I}G_i$: every point of $E$ lies in at least one $G_i$.

Requiring $G_i=E$ for every $i$ is far too strong; the $G_i$ need not equal $E$, just cover it.
$E\cap G_i=\varnothing$ for every $i$ would mean no $G_i$ meets $E$, the opposite of covering.
